title: Thermally induced conformational transition and binding affinity of beta-lactoglobulin and capsaicin: A multi-spectroscopic and molecular dynamics simulation study.
authors: Zhang, Dong; Cao, Jiaming; Duan, Min; Su, Chang; Yang, Li; Zhu, Yahui; Emara, A M; Gu, Xuedong; Tang, Jie; Yang, Lin
one_liner_zh: 该文结合多光谱与分子动力学模拟研究热诱导β-乳球蛋白构象转变及其与辣椒素的结合亲和力变化，虽以食品蛋白为对象，但MD模拟、对接及自由能分析等结构计算方法可迁移至蛋白质-配体结合研究，对蛋白质构象-结合关系建模有参考价值。
abstract: This study investigates the effect of heat treatment (25-95  degrees C) on the interaction between beta-lactoglobulin (beta-LG) and capsaicin (CAP) through multi-spectroscopic, physicochemical, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation approaches. We reveal a non-monotonic, temperature-dependent binding profile governed by beta-LG's multistage conformational transitions. Binding affinity increases from 25 to 65  degrees C, driven by a molten globule-like transition that exposes hydrophobic binding sites. A sharp decline at 75  degrees C, due to vigorous aggregation and site burial, marks a critical temperature threshold. Notably, partial binding recovery occurs at 85-95  degrees C, resulting from aggregate rearrangement. Beyond its role as a ligand, CAP actively modulates beta-LG aggregation by occupying hydrophobic patches, as evidenced by consistently smaller particle sizes and lower turbidity in CAP-supplemented groups. Molecular docking and MD simulations, including MM-PBSA free energy calculations and free energy landscape analysis, confirm stable binding within beta-LG's hydrophobic cavity and reveal that temperature-driven reshaping of conformational substates directly governs binding thermodynamics, with optimal affinity at 65  degrees C. These findings establish 65  degrees C as the optimal processing temperature for CAP retention, while suggesting that prolonged heating at 75  degrees C should be avoided. The strong correlations between simple physicochemical indicators (turbidity, solubility) and binding affinity offer a practical pathway for low-cost, real-time quality monitoring in industrial dairy processing.
abstract_zh: 本研究通过多光谱、物理化学及分子动力学（molecular dynamics, MD）模拟方法，探讨了热处理（25-95摄氏度）对β-乳球蛋白（beta-lactoglobulin, beta-LG）与辣椒素（capsaicin, CAP）之间相互作用的影响。我们揭示了一种由beta-LG多阶段构象转变所调控的非单调、温度依赖性结合特征。结合亲和力在25至65摄氏度范围内增强，这归因于熔球态样转变暴露了疏水结合位点。在75摄氏度时，由于剧烈聚集和位点埋藏，结合力急剧下降，标志着一个关键温度阈值。值得注意的是，在85-95摄氏度时，由于聚集体重排，结合部分恢复。除作为配体外，CAP还通过占据疏水斑块主动调节beta-LG聚集，这由CAP补充组中持续较小的粒径和较低的浊度所证实。分子对接和MD模拟，包括MM-PBSA自由能计算和自由能景观分析，确认了beta-LG疏水腔内的稳定结合，并揭示温度驱动的构象亚态重塑直接调控结合热力学，在65摄氏度时达到最佳亲和力。这些发现确定65摄氏度为CAP保留的最佳加工温度，同时建议应避免在75摄氏度下长时间加热。简单物理化学指标（浊度、溶解度）与结合亲和力之间的强相关性，为工业乳品加工中低成本、实时质量监测提供了一条实用途径。
